Answer: D
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) shows a well-circumscribed, radiolucent (fat-density) mass located anteriorly and attached to the inner aspect of the rib/sternum, which is characteristic of a parosteal lipoma. Its fat density distinguishes it from pulmonary nodules or solid tumors, and its bony attachment distinguishes it from subpleural lipomas.
